original_sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name
FROM customer c
WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey) > 20

candidates.sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name
FROM customer c
JOIN orders o ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
GROUP BY c.c_custkey, c.c_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 20
candidates.rationale: Replaces the correlated subquery with a single join and group-by, allowing the optimizer to use a hash join or index scan on orders.o_custkey instead of executing a subquery for every customer row.

candidates.sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name
FROM customer c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM orders o
  WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
  GROUP BY o.o_custkey
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 20
)
candidates.rationale: Uses EXISTS with a grouped subquery so the inner query can be evaluated once per distinct customer key rather than counting all matching rows for every outer row.

candidates.sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name
FROM customer c
JOIN (
  SELECT o_custkey, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY o_custkey
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 20
) o ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
candidates.rationale: Pre-aggregates the orders table in a derived table to find customer keys with more than 20 orders, then joins back to customer, avoiding per-row subquery execution.
